# pyRevit Extension Builder

> Design a pyRevit extension (Revit ribbon tabs, panels and buttons with their Python scripts) and download it as a ZIP ready to drop in pyRevit's extensions folder. Static site, no account, no server: everything happens in the browser.

pyRevit is the open-source Revit add-in framework (https://pyrevitlabs.io). An extension is a folder: `<name>.extension/<tab>.tab/<panel>.panel/<button>.<type>/`, each button folder holding a `bundle.yaml` of parameters, a `script.py` and icons. This builder writes those folders for you from a JSON description: the **extension spec**.

## How a language model uses it

1. **Write a spec** (format below; JSON Schema: https://builder.pyrevitlabs.io/api/extension.schema.json).
2. **Hand it to the user**, in one of three ways:
   - **An import link** (best for small and medium specs): `https://builder.pyrevitlabs.io/#spec=` followed by the spec's JSON, URL-encoded (JavaScript's `encodeURIComponent`). Opening it loads the extension in the builder, where the user checks it and clicks Download. Example: https://builder.pyrevitlabs.io/#spec=%7B%22name%22%3A%22Hello%22%2C%22tabs%22%3A%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22Hello%22%2C%22panels%22%3A%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22Tools%22%2C%22items%22%3A%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22pushbutton%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22Say%20Hi%22%2C%22script%22%3A%22print(%5C%22Hi%5C%22)%22%7D%5D%7D%5D%7D%5D%7D
   - **A link to a hosted file**: `https://builder.pyrevitlabs.io/?spec_url=<https URL of the JSON>` (the host must allow cross-origin reads, as GitHub raw files and gists do).
   - **A file**: give the JSON as `<name>.json`; the user opens it with the builder's Load button.
3. **Or act in the page yourself**, when you run in the user's browser:
   - with WebMCP, the page registers tools on `document.modelContext`: `get_extension_schema`, `get_extension`, `validate_extension`, `set_extension` (one undo step) and `download_extension`;
   - by script, the same tools are on `window.pyrevitBuilder`: `await pyrevitBuilder.call("set_extension", { spec })`, or `getExtension()`, `setExtension(spec)`, `validate(spec)`, `download()`, `schema()`.
   Edit by reading the extension, changing the JSON, and writing it back.

The builder checks a spec at two levels, and says what to fix:
- **errors**: the spec is malformed (wrong shape, unknown type or parameter, bad value, a bundle where pyRevit doesn't allow it), with the JSON path of each, e.g. `tabs[0].panels[1].items[2].type: Pulldown cannot contain Stack`. It is not opened at all.
- **problems**: it opens, but pyRevit would skip part of it (a one-row stack, two names making the same folder), so download is refused until they are fixed.
- **warnings** don't block anything, and say why: a button whose required parameter is empty (it downloads, and the reply names the buttons that won't work and what pyRevit will do with them), sample values still in place, a family file to add after unzipping.

A spec that brings its own `script` is opened only after the user has seen which buttons run custom Python.

## The extension spec (version 1)

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "name": "Acme Tools",
  "tabs": [
    {
      "name": "Acme",
      "panels": [
        {
          "name": "Sheets",
          "items": [
            {
              "type": "pushbutton",
              "name": "Renumber",
              "title": "Renumber\nSheets",
              "tooltip": "Renumber the selected sheets in order.",
              "author": "Acme BIM",
              "context": "selection",
              "script": "from pyrevit import revit\nprint(len(revit.get_selection()))"
            },
            {
              "type": "stack",
              "name": "Help",
              "items": [
                {
                  "type": "urlbutton",
                  "name": "Docs",
                  "hyperlink": "https://pyrevitlabs.io"
                },
                {
                  "type": "toggle",
                  "name": "Auto Save",
                  "tooltip": "Turn auto save on or off."
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "pulldown",
              "name": "Export",
              "items": [
                {
                  "type": "pushbutton",
                  "name": "To PDF",
                  "min_revit_version": 2024
                },
                {
                  "type": "pushbutton",
                  "name": "To DWG",
                  "engine_clean": true
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `name`, then `tabs` → `panels` → `items`, each list in ribbon order.
- Every bundle has a `type` and a `name` (its folder name: unique among its siblings, ignoring case). `title` is the text under the icon (`\n` breaks the line; default: the name); `tooltip` shows on hover.
- Fill every required parameter (in bold below): nothing is filled in for you, and a button without one won't work in Revit.
- `script` is the Python of `script.py` (pyRevit runs IronPython by default; `from pyrevit import revit, DB, forms, script`). Leave it out for a starter script.
- `icon`, `icon_dark`, `icon_on` are PNG data URLs (`data:image/png;base64,...`, ideally 96x96). Leave them out for the pyRevit icon.
- A stack holds 2 or 3 bundles; pyRevit drops a stack with one. A pulldown or split button holds commands, not stacks or other groups. A `nobutton` only goes in a pulldown or split button, never directly in a panel.
- A `content` button loads a Revit family: the user puts the `.rfa` file named in `content` into its folder after unzipping.
- Only the parameters listed for a type are accepted. Yes/no parameters are `true`/`false`; versions are numbers.

## Bundle types

| type | folder | what it is | items it holds | parameters (**required**) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pushbutton` | .pushbutton | Push Button:  |  | context, engine_clean, engine_full_frame, engine_persistent, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, script, icon, icon_dark |
| `toggle` | .smartbutton | Toggle:  |  | context, engine_clean, engine_full_frame, engine_persistent, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, script, icon, icon_dark, icon_on |
| `panelbutton` | .panelbutton | Panel Button:  |  | engine_clean, engine_full_frame, engine_persistent, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, script, icon, icon_dark |
| `urlbutton` | .urlbutton | URL Button:  |  | **hyperlink**, context, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, icon, icon_dark |
| `content` | .content | Content Button: Needs a content.rfa family in this folder. |  | **content**, content_alt, context, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, icon, icon_dark |
| `pulldown` | .pulldown | Pulldown:  | pushbutton, toggle, panelbutton, urlbutton, content, linkbutton, invokebutton, nobutton | context, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta |
| `splitbutton` | .splitbutton | Split Button:  | pushbutton, toggle, panelbutton, urlbutton, content, linkbutton, invokebutton, nobutton | context, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta |
| `splitpushbutton` | .splitpushbutton | Split Push Button:  | pushbutton, toggle, panelbutton, urlbutton, content, linkbutton, invokebutton, nobutton | context, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta |
| `stack` | .stack | Stack:  | pushbutton, toggle, urlbutton, content, linkbutton, invokebutton, pulldown, splitbutton, splitpushbutton |  |
| `combobox` | .combobox | Combo Box:  |  | **members**, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta |
| `linkbutton` | .linkbutton | Link Button: Binds to a .NET class. For a web link, use URL Button. |  | **assembly**, **command_class**, availability_class, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, icon, icon_dark |
| `invokebutton` | .invokebutton | Invoke Button: Runs a .NET assembly; the command class is optional. |  | **assembly**, command_class, availability_class, large_icon, author, help_url, min_revit_version, max_revit_version, highlight, beta, icon, icon_dark |
| `nobutton` | .nobutton | No Button: A script bundle with no ribbon button. |  | author, engine_clean, engine_full_frame, engine_persistent, min_revit_version, max_revit_version |

## Parameters

- `author`: Shown in the button's tooltip, and written as __author__ in its script. Values: text.
- `help_url`: Opened when the user presses F1 over the button. Values: a URL.
- `hyperlink`: The page a URL Button opens in the browser. Values: a URL.
- `assembly`: The compiled .NET assembly (no .dll), resolved from this bundle's bin/ or Revit's add-ins. Values: text.
- `command_class`: Namespace-qualified IExternalCommand class to run. Values: text.
- `availability_class`: IExternalCommandAvailability class deciding when the button is enabled. Values: text.
- `content`: The .rfa family the button loads. Add the file to the bundle folder after unzipping. Values: text.
- `content_alt`: An alternative family loaded on Ctrl+Click. Values: text.
- `members`: The combo box's items, as a YAML list; each needs an id and a text. Values: a YAML list, or [{"id": "...", "text": "..."}].
- `context`: When the button is enabled. With none, it always is. Values: "", "zero-doc", "selection", "doc-project", "doc-family", "active-floor-plan", "active-3d-view", "active-detail-view", "active-drafting-view".
- `min_revit_version`: Older Revit versions skip this button. Values: a year, 2021-2028.
- `max_revit_version`: Newer Revit versions skip this button. Values: a year, 2021-2028.
- `engine_clean` (bundle.yaml: engine.clean): Run in a fresh engine every time instead of a cached one. Values: true/false.
- `engine_full_frame` (bundle.yaml: engine.full_frame): IronPython full-frame mode, needed by some libraries. Values: true/false.
- `engine_persistent` (bundle.yaml: engine.persistent): Keep the engine alive after the script ends, for scripts that leave windows open. Values: true/false.
- `large_icon`: Use the large icon size where Revit would use the medium one, in stacks and lists. Values: true/false.
- `highlight`: Revit's orange dot marking a new or updated button. Values: "", "new", "updated".
- `beta` (bundle.yaml: is_beta): Hidden unless the user turns on beta tools in pyRevit's settings. Values: true/false.
